paragraphs: In this Annual Report on Form 10-K, when we use the terms the "Company," "Clipper Realty," "we," "us," or "our," unless the context otherwise requires, we are referring to Clipper Realty Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. Certain disclosures included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K constitute forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. See Item 1A, "Risk Factors," and "Cautionary Note Concerning Forward-Looking Statements."

Clipper Realty Inc. is a self-administered and self-managed real estate company that acquires, owns, manages, operates and repositions multifamily residential and commercial properties in the New York metropolitan area, with a portfolio in Manhattan and Brooklyn. We were formed to continue and expand the commercial real estate business of the 50/53 JV LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, Renaissance Equity Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, Berkshire Equity LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, and Gunki Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (collectively referred to as, the "Predecessor" or the "predecessor entities"). These predecessor entities were formed by principals of our management team from 2002 to 2014. Our primary focus is to continue to own, manage and operate our portfolio, and to acquire and re-position additional multifamily residential and commercial properties in the New York metropolitan area.

We were incorporated in the State of Maryland on July 7, 2015. On August 3, 2015, we closed a private offering of shares of our common stock, in which we raised net proceeds of approximately $130.2 million. In connection with the private offering, we consummated a series of investment and other formation transactions that were designed, among other things, to enable us to qualify as a real estate investment trust, or a "REIT," for U.S. federal income tax purposes, and we elected to be treated as a REIT commencing with the taxable year ended December 31, 2015. We contributed the net proceeds of the private offering to Clipper Realty L.P., our operating partnership subsidiary, or the "Operating Partnership,", in exchange for units in the Operating Partnership.

On February 9, 2017, we priced an initial public offering, or the "IPO," of 6,390,149 primary shares of our common stock (including the exercise of the over-allotment option, which closed on March 10, 2017). The net proceeds of the IPO were approximately $78.7 million. We contributed the proceeds of the IPO to the Operating Partnership, in exchange for units in the Operating Partnership.
As of December 31, 2025, the properties owned by the Company consisted of the following:

Tribeca House in Manhattan, comprising two buildings, one with 21 stories and one with 12 stories, containing residential and retail space with an aggregate of approximately 483,000 square feet of residential rental Gross Leasable Area ("GLA") and 77,000 square feet of retail rental and parking GLA;
Flatbush Gardens in Brooklyn, a 59-building residential housing complex with 2,494 rentable units and approximately 1,749,000 square feet of residential rental GLA;
141 Livingston Street in Brooklyn, a 15-story office building with approximately 216,000 square feet of GLA;
250 Livingston Street in Brooklyn, a 12-story office and residential building with approximately 370,000 square feet of GLA (fully remeasured);

Aspen in Manhattan, a 7-story building containing residential and retail space with approximately 166,000 square feet of residential rental GLA and approximately 21,000 square feet of retail rental GLA;
Clover House in Brooklyn, an 11-story residential building with approximately 102,000 square feet of residential rental GLA;
1010 Pacific Street in Brooklyn, a 9-story residential building with approximately 119,000 square feet of residential rental GLA; and
The Dean Street property in Brooklyn, a 9-story residential building with approximately 160,000 square feet of residential rental GLA and approximately 9,000 square feet of retail rental GLA.

On May 30, 2025, the Company completed the sale of 10 West 65th Street in Manhattan, a 6-story residential building with approximately 76,000 square feet of residential rental GLA. for gross proceeds of $45,500. The Company incurred $1,900 in closing costs and paid $800 in accrued interest at closing. At closing, the Company repaid in full its $31,200 mortgage note (the "Mortgage") with Flagstar Bank ("Flagstar") (see note 4 below). The Company recorded a loss on the disposal of long-lived assets of $857 and a loss on impairment of long-lived assets of $33,780 during the year-ended December 31, 2025.

headings: Risks Related to Real Estate
Our portfolio's revenue is currently generated from eight properties.

We may be unable to renew leases or lease currently vacant space on favorable terms or at all as leases expire or terminate, which could adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations and cash flow.
We engage in development and redevelopment activities, which could expose us to different risks that could adversely affect us, including our financial condition, cash flow and results of operations.
Our dependence on rental revenue may adversely affect us, including our profitability, our ability to meet our debt obligations and our ability to make distributions to our stockholders.
Reimbursements from government agencies under the Article 11 Agreement might be lower than expected and costs to implement the mandatory capital improvements might be higher than expected.
Real estate investments are relatively illiquid and may limit our flexibility.

Competition could limit our ability to acquire attractive investment opportunities and increase the costs of those opportunities, which may adversely affect us, including our profitability, and impede our growth.
Competition may impede our ability to attract or retain tenants or re-lease space, which could adversely affect our results of operations and cash flow.
We are subject to potential losses that are either uninsurable, not economically insurable or that are in excess of our insurance coverage.
We are subject to risks from natural disasters such as severe weather.
Actual or threatened terrorist attacks may adversely affect our ability to generate revenues and the value of our properties.

We may become subject to liability relating to environmental and health and safety matters, which could have an adverse effect on us, including our financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.
We may acquire properties or portfolios of properties through tax-deferred contribution transactions, which could result in stockholder dilution and limit our ability to sell such assets.
paragraphs: Set forth below are certain risk factors that could harm our business, results of operations and financial condition. You should carefully read the following risk factors, together with the financial statements, related notes and other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Our business, financial condition and operating results may suffer if any of the following risks are realized. If any of these risks or uncertainties occur, the trading price of our common stock could decline and you might lose all or part of your investment. This Annual Report on Form 10-K contains forward-looking statements that involve risks see "Cautionary Note Concerning Forward-Looking Statements."

Our dependency on two commercial leases with certain agencies of the City of New York (NYC), as a single government tenant in our office buildings, with one lease having terminated effective August 23, 2025, and the other lease having expired on December 27, 2025 and our inability to replace NYC as a tenant at rent rates comparable to the rates in the lease that terminated in August 2025 or to enter into a five-year extension of the lease that expired in December 2025 could cause a material adverse effect on us, including our financial condition, results of operations and cash flow.

Our rental revenue depends on entering into leases with and collecting rents from tenants. As of December 31, 2025, Kings County Court, the Human Resources Administration, and the Department of Environmental Protection, all of which are agencies of the City of New York, occupied all 206,084 of rentable square feet at 141 Livingston Street and terminated its lease and vacated all 342,496 rentable square feet of commercial space at our 250 Livingston Street. The commercial rental space at 141 Livingston is occupied subject to hold-over rent provisions in the lease that expired on December 27, 2025. Our commercial leases with the City of New York comprised approximately 18% and 22% of total revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. We are also subject to covenants covering these leases in our loan agreements related to our commercial office properties located at 250 Livingston Street and 141 Livingston Street.

As of February 23, 2024, The City of New York, a municipal corporation acting through the Department of Citywide Administrative Services ("NYC"), notified us of its intention to terminate its lease at 250 Livingston Street effective August 23, 2025, and they vacated the space on that date. The lease generally provided for rent payments in the amount of $15.4 million per annum. We have been unable to replace NYC as a tenant, and we may continue to be unable to replace it with other commercial tenants at comparable rent rates or at all, may incur substantial costs to improve the vacated space or may have to offer significant inducements to fill the space, all of which may have an adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations and cash flow.

Our subsidiary, 250 Livingston Owner LLC ("Borrower"), entered into the Loan Agreement, dated as of May 31, 2019 (the "Loan Agreement"), with Citi Real Estate Funding Inc., related to a loan in the principal amount of $125.0 million (the "Loan"). The Loan is evidenced by certain promissory notes (the "Notes") and secured by our 250 Livingston Street property in Brooklyn, New York (the "Property"). We and our Operating Partnership serve as guarantors of certain obligations under the Loan.

On March 18, 2025, we were notified by legal counsel to the servicer for the loan related to the 250 Livingston Street property that, due to the failure of our subsidiary, 250 Livingston Owner LLC, to cause all revenue generated by the 250 Livingston Street property to be deposited into the cash management account as required by the loan agreement related to the $125 million building mortgage loan, an event of default occurred under the $125 million building mortgage loan. The notice provided that if the 250 Livingston Owner LLC fails to cure the event of default, the lender may, among other things, accelerate the $125 million building mortgage loan and demand all amounts owing to the lender to be immediately payable, institute proceedings for the foreclosure of all liens securing the loan and sell the 250 Livingston Street Property, or file a lawsuit against the 250 Livingston owner LLC or the guarantors. As of May 12, 2025, we have complied with the lender's requirement to have the deposits made by all tenants deposited directly into the cash management account. On May 8, 2025, we transferred $6.3 million to the cash management account to cover amounts owed prior to the activation of the cash management account. On May 15, 2025, legal counsel for the lender notified us that they allege that we are in default on the $125 million mortgage loan due to its allegation that we, as the guarantor, did not maintain a net worth of not less than $100 million as of December 31, 2024, as required under the loan agreement. We replied to the lender disputing such calculation and alleging that the lender did not calculate net worth in a reasonable manner and provided our lender with our own calculation of net worth that shows a net worth in excess of the required amount. On May 28, 2025, the lender replied to us concurring with us and notifying us that they agree that we are compliant with the $100 million requirement. On July 28, 2025, we were notified by legal counsel for the lender that they alleged that we were once again in default for failure to remit all revenue derived from 250 Livingston into the cash management account. We responded by disputing the allegations in May 8, 2025, letter and noting all rents from the tenants have been deposited into the cash management account.

paragraphs: 本年度報表（Form 10-K）中，當我們使用 "本公司"、"Clipper Realty"、"我們"、"我們" 或 "我們" 這些詞彙時，除非上下文另有說明，否則我們指的是 Clipper Realty Inc. 及其合併子公司。本年度報表中包含某些揭露資訊屬於前瞻性陳述，這些陳述受到風險與不確定性影響。請參閱第 1A 項 "風險因素"，以及 "前瞻性陳述警示說明"。

Clipper Realty Inc. 是一家自營且自管的不動產公司，專門取得、擁有、管理、營運及重新定位位於紐約都會區的多單位住宅及商業不動產，其資產組合涵蓋曼哈頓與布魯克林。我們成立的目的是繼續並擴展 50/53 JV LLC（一家特拉華州有限責任公司）、Renaissance Equity Holdings LLC（一家特拉華州有限責任公司）、Berkshire Equity LLC（一家特拉華州有限責任公司）及 Gunki Holdings LLC（一家特拉華州有限責任公司）的商業不動產業務（ collectively referred to as, the "Predecessor" or the "predecessor entities"）。這些前身公司是由我們管理團隊的高層於 2002 年至 2014 年間成立。我們的主要重點是繼續擁有、管理及營運我們的資產組合，並取得及重新定位紐約都會區的更多多單位住宅及商業不動產。

我們於 2015 年 7 月 7 日在馬裏蘭州註冊成立。2015 年 8 月 3 日，我們完成一項私人發行，發行我們的普通股股份，並籌得約 130.2 百萬美元的淨資金。配合此次私人發行，我們完成一系列投資及其他設立交易，其目的包括，但不僅限於，使我們符合美國聯邦所得稅法的不動產投資信託（REIT）資格，並於 2015 年 12 月 31 日結止的課稅年度開始，我們選擇被視為 REIT。我們將私人發行的淨資金貢獻至我們的營運合夥企業子公司 Clipper Realty L.P.，或稱為 "營運合夥企業"，以交換營運合夥企業的單位。
2017 年 2 月 9 日，我們定價一項首次公開發行（IPO），發行 6,390,149 股我們的普通股股份（包含行使過量發行權的股份，該過量發行權於 2017 年 3 月 10 日完成）。此次 IPO 的淨資金約為 78.7 百萬美元。我們將 IPO 的資金貢獻至營運合夥企業，以交換營運合夥企業的單位。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司所擁有的不動產如下：
曼哈頓的 Tribeca House，包含兩棟大樓，一棟為 21 層，另一棟為 12 層，內含住宅與零售空間，總計約 483,000 平方英呎的住宅租賃可出租面積（GLA）及 77,000 平方英呎的零售租賃及停車 GLA；
布魯克林的 Flatbush Gardens，為一個包含 59 棟住宅大樓的住宅複合社區，擁有 2,494 個可出租單位及約 1,749,000 平方英呎的住宅租賃 GLA；
布魯克林的 141 Livingston Street，為一棟 15 層的辦公大樓，擁有約 216,000 平方英呎的 GLA；
250 Livingston Street 在布魯克林，為一棟 12 層的辦公與住宅大樓，總樓地板面積約為 370,000 平方英呎（已重新測量）；
Aspen 在曼哈頓，為一棟 7 層的建築物，包含住宅與零售空間，住宅租賃樓地板面積約為 166,000 平方英呎，零售租賃樓地板面積約為 21,000 平方英呎；
Clover House 在布魯克林，為一棟 11 層的住宅大樓，住宅租賃樓地板面積約為 102,000 平方英呎；
1010 Pacific Street 在布魯克林，為一棟 9 層的住宅大樓，住宅租賃樓地板面積約為 119,000 平方英呎；以及
布魯克林的 Dean Street 不動產，為一棟 9 層的住宅大樓，住宅租賃樓地板面積約為 160,000 平方英呎，零售租賃樓地板面積約為 9,000 平方英呎。

2025 年 5 月 30 日，本公司完成出售 10 West 65th Street 在曼哈頓的住宅大樓，為一棟 6 層的住宅大樓，住宅租賃樓地板面積約為 76,000 平方英呎，總計售出金額為 45,500 美元。本公司於交易結清時產生 1,900 美元的結清費用，並支付 800 美元的應計利息。於結清時，本公司以 31,200 美元償還其 Flagstar Bank（"Flagstar"）的抵押貸款（"Mortgage"）（請參閱下文第 4 節）。本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日結算年度內，記錄長期資產處置損失 857 美元，以及長期資產減損損失 33,780 美元。

headings: 與不動產相關的風險
本公司資產組合的營業收入目前來自八處不動產。
我們可能無法在有利條件下或完全無法續約或出租目前空置的空間，一旦租約到期或終止，這可能會對我們的財務狀況、營運結果及現金流產生不利影響。
我們從事開發及重建活動，這可能會使我們面臨不同的風險，這些風險可能會對我們產生不利影響，包括財務狀況、現金流及營運結果。
我們對租金收入的依賴可能會對我們產生不利影響，包括利潤率、履行債務義務的能力及向股東發放紅利的能力。
根據第11條協議，政府機構的補償金額可能低於預期，而實施強制性資本改善的費用可能高於預期。
不動產投資相對缺乏流動性，可能會限制我們的靈活性。
競爭可能會限制我們取得具吸引力投資機會的能力，並提高這些機會的成本，這可能會對我們產生不利影響，包括利潤率，並阻礙我們的成長。
競爭可能妨礙本公司吸引或留住租戶或重新出租空間的能力，這可能會對本公司的營運成果及現金流產生不利影響。
本公司可能面臨無法投保、投保不經濟或超出本公司保險範圍的潛在損失。
本公司可能因自然災害如極端天氣等風險而遭受影響。
實際或威脅性的恐怖攻擊可能影響本公司產生收入的能力及不動產價值。
本公司可能因環境及健康安全事項而面臨責任，這可能會對本公司產生不利影響，包括財務狀況、現金流及營運成果。
本公司可能透過稅務延後認列交易取得不動產或不動產組合，這可能會導致股東稀釋並限制本公司出售這些資產的能力。
paragraphs: 下列為可能影響本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況之風險因素，請謹慎閱讀下列風險因素，並與財務報表、相關附註及其他資訊一併參考。若任何下列風險因素實現，本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果可能受影響。若任何上述風險或不確定性發生，本公司普通股之交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。本年度報告表10-K包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險，請參閱「關於前瞻性陳述之警示說明」。
本公司對兩項商業租賃之依賴，租賃對象為紐約市（NYC）之某些機構，作為本公司辦公大樓之單一政府租戶，其中一項租賃於2025年8月23日終止，另一項租賃於2025年12月27日到期，且本公司無法以與2025年8月終止租賃之租金率相當之租金率取代NYC作為租戶，或與2025年12月到期租賃簽訂五年期延長租賃，可能對本公司造成重大不利影響，包括財務狀況、營運成果及現金流。

本公司之租金收入取決於與租戶簽訂租賃契約並收取租金。截至2025年12月31日，Kings County Court、Human Resources Administration及Department of Environmental Protection，皆為紐約市之機構，佔據了141 Livingston Street之全部206,084平方呎可出租空間，並於2025年12月27日終止租賃，並離開了250 Livingston Street之全部342,496平方呎商業空間。141 Livingston Street之商業租賃空間係根據2025年12月27日到期租賃之延長租金條款佔據。本公司與紐約市之商業租賃契約，於2025年及2024年財務年度分別佔總營收約18%及22%。本公司亦受貸款契約中關於這些租賃之約束條款所限制，貸款契約與本公司位於250 Livingston Street及141 Livingston Street之商業辦公大樓有關。

截至2024年2月23日，紐約市（作為紐約市行政服務部（"NYC"）之市政公司）通知本公司，其意圖於2025年8月23日終止250 Livingston Street之租賃，並於該日期離開該空間。租賃一般規定每年租金為15.4百萬美元。本公司無法取代NYC作為租戶，且可能持續無法以相當租金率或其他商業租戶取代，可能需支出大量費用改善該空間，或需提供重大誘因以填滿空間，所有這些都可能對本公司財務狀況、營運成果及現金流造成不利影響。

本公司之子公司250 Livingston Owner LLC（"Borrower"）於2019年5月31日與Citi Real Estate Funding Inc.簽訂貸款協議（"Loan Agreement"），與一筆本金為125.0百萬美元（"Loan"）之貸款有關。貸款由若干本票（"Notes"）證明，並以本公司位於紐約市布魯克林之250 Livingston Street不動產（"Property"）為擔保。本公司及其營運合夥人為貸款相關義務之擔保人。

2025年3月18日，本公司收到貸款相關貸款機構之法律顧問通知，因本公司子公司250 Livingston Owner LLC未能使250 Livingston Street不動產所產生之所有收入依貸款協議之規定存入現金管理帳戶，導致貸款協議下之違約事件發生。通知指出，若250 Livingston Owner LLC未能解決此違約事件，貸款機構可依貸款協議，加速償還125百萬美元之貸款，並要求所有應付款項立即支付，或對貸款之擔保權進行拍賣並出售250 Livingston Street不動產，或對250 Livingston Owner LLC或擔保人提起訴訟。截至2025年5月12日，本公司已符合貸款機構之要求，使所有租戶之存款直接存入現金管理帳戶。2025年5月8日，本公司將6.3百萬美元轉入現金管理帳戶，以覆蓋現金管理帳戶啟用前應付款項。2025年5月15日，貸款機構之法律顧問通知本公司，其聲稱本公司因未維持截至2024年12月31日淨值不低於100百萬美元，而違反貸款協議。本公司回覆貸款機構，爭議此計算方式，並聲稱貸款機構未以合理方式計算淨值，並提供本公司自行計算之淨值，顯示淨值高於所需金額。2025年5月28日，貸款機構回覆本公司，同意本公司符合100百萬美元之要求。2025年7月28日，本公司收到貸款機構之法律顧問通知，聲稱本公司因未將250 Livingston 之所有收入轉入現金管理帳戶，再次違反貸款協議。本公司於2025年5月8日回覆爭議此聲稱，並指出所有租戶之租金已存入現金管理帳戶。
